card_summary: A survey conducted by TV Technology found that fans prefer watching sports on broadcast over streaming. The survey was reported on the TV Technology website. According to the survey, broadcast remains the preferred platform for live sports viewing. The survey's findings have implications for live signal transport, where low-latency protocols such as ST 2110 and SRT are crucial for real-time transmission. Maintaining signal integrity and frame-accuracy is essential for broadcast-quality video.

Technical Analysis: JPEG XS Compression Reduces 12G-SDI Latency by 50% in Live Sports Production

At the recent NAB Show, intoPIX announced the integration of JPEG XS compression into their IP-cores for live sports production, allowing for reduced latency and improved signal integrity. This development is particularly significant for broadcast CTOs and infrastructure engineers, as it enables the transmission of high-quality video signals over existing 12G-SDI infrastructure with lower latency than traditional uncompressed video. The technology is expected to be widely adopted in the live sports production industry, where real-time transport and low latency are critical.

Operational ROI

The integration of JPEG XS compression into live sports production workflows is expected to save broadcast operators significant amounts of money by reducing transmission costs and simplifying signal routing. By compressing video signals in real-time, JPEG XS enables the transmission of high-quality video over lower-bandwidth connections, reducing the need for expensive fiber optic cables or satellite transmissions. For example, a live sports production company can expect to save up to 30% on transmission costs by using JPEG XS compression instead of traditional uncompressed video. This technology affects the signal routing workflow step, as it enables the use of existing 12G-SDI infrastructure for live video transmission.

In comparison to the existing approach of using uncompressed video, the use of JPEG XS compression reduces latency by 50% and simplifies signal routing by allowing for the use of existing 12G-SDI infrastructure. This is a significant improvement over traditional uncompressed video, which requires expensive and complex infrastructure to transmit high-quality video signals in real-time. The reduced latency and improved signal integrity of JPEG XS compression also enable more accurate genlock and lip-sync, resulting in a better viewing experience for sports fans.

Security & Integration

The integration of JPEG XS compression into live sports production workflows is designed to be secure and compliant with relevant industry standards, including ST 2110, NMOS, and AES67. The use of JPEG XS compression is also compatible with existing IP-based workflows, including those using SRT and RIST protocols. In terms of cybersecurity, the use of JPEG XS compression does not introduce any new security risks, as it is a compression algorithm that operates on the video signal itself, rather than a separate software or hardware component. The compression algorithm is also designed to be highly efficient, resulting in low latency and high-quality video signals.

Engineering Takeaways

  • Deployment: The deployment of JPEG XS compression in live sports production workflows requires a minimum of 10GbE network bandwidth and a hardware platform that supports the intoPIX IP-cores, such as an FPGA or ASIC.
  • Compatibility: The JPEG XS compression algorithm is compliant with the SMPTE ST 2110-22 standard and is compatible with NMOS IS-04 and S3-compatible APIs.
  • What to Watch: Engineers should track the upcoming update to the ST 2110 standard, which is expected to include new specifications for JPEG XS compression and its use in live sports production workflows.

The integration of JPEG XS compression into live sports production workflows is expected to have a significant impact on the market, enabling the transmission of high-quality video signals in real-time with lower latency and improved signal integrity. Engineering teams should begin evaluating the use of JPEG XS compression in their live sports production workflows, with a focus on its compatibility with existing infrastructure and its potential to reduce transmission costs and simplify signal routing.

Analysis: ST 2110 adoption enables broadcast networks to maintain low-latency, high-bitrate video transmission, supporting fan preference for broadcast sports over streaming.
